content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
content.topic: The importance of self-discipline in students' personal growth

modelEssay.title: The Importance of Self-Discipline in Personal Growth
modelEssay.content:
Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth. In an age of endless distractions, the ability to govern oneself has become a decisive factor that separates those who merely dream from those who genuinely achieve.

Self-discipline matters for two reasons. First, it transforms vague intentions into consistent action. A student who sets a study schedule and sticks to it, even when tempted by short videos or games, gradually accumulates knowledge that others lose to procrastination. Second, it cultivates resilience. By repeatedly choosing long-term goals over instant gratification, students build the mental strength to persevere through setbacks. Take my roommate as an example: by rising early to review lessons every day, he turned average grades into a scholarship within a single year.

In conclusion, self-discipline is not a restriction but a form of freedom—the freedom to become who we aspire to be. The earlier students master it, the more steadily they will grow.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development.
transcript.translation: 幼儿看电视时间增加长期以来与一些发展领域的进展较差有关。

transcript.text: One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen.
transcript.translation: 对抗这些负面影响的一种可能方法是在观看屏幕时交谈。

transcript.text: As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers, during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten.
transcript.translation: 正如一项新研究表明，在电视时间，父母与学龄前儿童进行对话越多，这些孩子在进入幼儿园时好奇心水平可能越高。

transcript.text: This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
transcript.translation: 这对于具有社会经济劣势的儿童尤其如此。

transcript.text: Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity, said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C.S.
transcript.translation: 密歇根大学健康中心C.S. Mott儿童医院的主要作者Prachi Shah说，我们的发现强调了父母对话对促进早期儿童发展和好奇心的重要性。

transcript.text: Mott Children's Hospital.
transcript.translation: Mott儿童医院。

transcript.text: Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent screen time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers, and then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten.
transcript.translation: 研究人员评估了1,500名学龄前儿童每天的电视接触时间以及父母在屏幕时间对话的频率，然后测量了幼儿园中的早期儿童好奇心。

transcript.text: The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten, and behavioral developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status.
transcript.translation: 该研究特别关注好奇心水平，这与幼儿园中增强的学习能力以及更高的阅读和数学学业成就，以及行为发展益处相关，尤其是对于来自社会经济地位较低家庭的儿童。

transcript.text: While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones, television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time.
transcript.translation: 虽然许多幼儿现在通过平板电脑和手机等移动设备接触数字媒体成长，但电视仍然是主导的屏幕活动，占所有屏幕时间的72%。

transcript.text: TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
transcript.translation: 电视存在于98%的家庭中，使得电视接触成为幼儿相关的发展背景。

transcript.text: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids.
transcript.translation: 过度的媒体接触，包括电视，可能会取代探索性活动，如游戏和亲子互动，这些活动被认为是培养孩子好奇心的关键。

transcript.text: Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children, including while watching television, Shah said.
transcript.translation: Shah说，我们的发现表明，父母在日常生活中寻找机会促进与幼儿的对话交流非常重要，包括在看电视时。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第2段。

transcript.text: Humans are aspirational, goal-seeking beings.
transcript.translation: 人类是具有抱负、追求目标的生物。

transcript.text: Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire.
transcript.translation: 根据研究，我们每个人都有天生的获取驱动力。

transcript.text: The dark side of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more things, and to socially compare our stuff with all the stuff other people have in their lives.
transcript.translation: 这种获取驱动力的阴暗面是盲目地被驱使去拥有越来越多的东西，并与他人生活中拥有的所有东西进行社会比较。

transcript.text: So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?
transcript.translation: 因此问题是，我们如何确保以积极的方式利用我们的获取驱动力，从而有益于我们的幸福？

transcript.text: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational.
transcript.translation: 一种方法是变得更加有意地追求抱负。

transcript.text: To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life.
transcript.translation: 有意追求抱负包括有意识地渴望成为在职业和个人生活中成功所需的人。

transcript.text: It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being.
transcript.translation: 它还包括有意识地渴望在生活中获取能积极影响你幸福感的东西。

transcript.text: If you're not consciously, mindfully, and intentionally conscious of your inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
transcript.translation: 如果你没有有意识地、专注地、有意地意识到你天生的获取驱动力，你可能会盲目地追求所有错误的东西。

transcript.text: While your intentional aspirational goals will include the pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
transcript.translation: 虽然你的有意追求抱负的目标将包括追求能增加你幸福感的东西，但它们也应该包括在你各种生活角色中帮助他人的目标。

transcript.text: Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best, a person of good character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
transcript.translation: 你的有意追求抱负的目标还将包括努力成为最好的自己，一个具有良好品格、正直和值得信赖的人。

transcript.text: Think about this from a practical rather than theoretical viewpoint.
transcript.translation: 从实际而非理论的角度来思考这一点。

transcript.text: If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for.
transcript.translation: 如果你不追求有意追求抱负的目标，你就没有奋斗的方向。

transcript.text: If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you'll not be able to experience, live, and enjoy all that life has to offer.
transcript.translation: 如果你没有奋斗的方向，你就将自己置于一个危险的位置，只是随波逐流地度过人生，你将无法体验、生活和享受生活所提供的一切。

transcript.text: It's revision time for exams and dissertations.
transcript.translation: 现在是考试和论文的复习时间。

transcript.text: The pressure is on, so you'll want all the help you can get to aid your memory and raise your grades.

transcript.text: As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime.

transcript.text: So, what brain-boosting food and drink would I recommend?
transcript.translation: 那么，我会推荐哪些促进大脑功能的食物和饮料呢？

transcript.text: Coffee can have numerous benefits.
transcript.translation: 咖啡有许多好处。

transcript.text: However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short-lived.
transcript.translation: 然而，虽然咖啡可能让你更清醒，但个体会产生耐受性，这意味着效果是短暂的。

transcript.text: Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy.
transcript.translation: 咖啡还会增加血糖，最终导致注意力不集中和缺乏精力。

transcript.text: It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee.
transcript.translation: 值得注意的是，人们对咖啡的反应各不相同。

transcript.text: Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount.
transcript.translation: 有些人可以在午夜喝咖啡后直接入睡，而另一些人在少量饮用后会感到焦虑。

transcript.text: Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home.
transcript.translation: 还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里自制的咖啡更浓。

transcript.text: So stop drinking coffee by 2 p.m.
transcript.translation: 因此，在下午2点后停止喝咖啡。

transcript.text: and have a maximum of two cups of coffee a day, but be aware of your own reaction to it.
transcript.translation: 每天最多喝两杯咖啡，但要注意自己对它的反应。

transcript.text: Whole-grain foods will ward off hunger.
transcript.translation: 全谷物食物能抵御饥饿。

transcript.text: Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread.
transcript.translation: 例子包括粥和全麦面包。

transcript.text: Combining whole-grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration.
transcript.translation: 将全谷物食物与蛋白质结合有助于保持血糖平衡，这对情绪和注意力至关重要。

transcript.text: Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack.
transcript.translation: 浆果和坚果是一种方便且营养丰富的零食。

transcript.text: Blueberries, like many dark-colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline.
transcript.translation: 蓝莓，像许多深色水果和蔬菜一样，可以减缓大脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。

transcript.text: Frozen berries are also a good choice.
transcript.translation: 冷冻浆果也是一个好选择。

transcript.text: They are usually cheap, last longer, and don't lose their nutrients when frozen.
transcript.translation: 它们通常便宜，保存时间更长，冷冻时不会失去营养。

transcript.text: But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy, as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
transcript.translation: 但调味和裹衣坚果不太健康，因为它们含有添加的油、盐和糖。

transcript.text: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need, but I would say food should always come before supplements.
transcript.translation: 医生常推荐服用维生素补充剂来补充所需营养，但我想说食物应始终优先于补充剂。

transcript.text: And the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet with lots of different colors, such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables.
transcript.translation: 尽可能获取多种营养的关键是吃多样化的饮食，包含多种不同颜色的食物，如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。

transcript.text: It's better to get everything you need from food and drink.
transcript.translation: 最好从食物和饮料中获取所需的一切。

transcript.text: For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C, which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.
transcript.translation: 例如，橙子不仅含有增强免疫系统的维生素C，还含有纤维和其他无法在一片药丸中同时获得的成分。

transcript.text: Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25%, and can elevate your mood as well.
transcript.translation: 不要忘记喝适量的水，这可以将注意力提高近25%，并提升情绪。

transcript.text: Finally, don't skip meals.

transcript.text: Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.

transcript.text: Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend.
transcript.translation: 汉斯·罗斯林发现了一个令人担忧的趋势。

transcript.text: Not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite.
transcript.translation: 不仅许多发达经济体的人们不知道世界正在变得更好，而且他们甚至认为情况恰恰相反。

transcript.text: This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars and famines.
transcript.translation: 这不足为奇，因为新闻专注于报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒。

transcript.text: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the $2 a day poverty line?
transcript.translation: 谁想听到这样一个事实：每天全世界约有20万人摆脱了每日2美元的贫困线？

transcript.text: Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day?
transcript.translation: 或者，每天有超过30万人首次获得电力和清洁水？

transcript.text: These stories of people in low-income countries simply don't make for exciting news coverage.
transcript.translation: 这些低收入国家人们的故事根本无法成为令人兴奋的新闻报道。

transcript.text: But, as Rosling pointed out in his book, Factfulness, it's important to put all the bad news in perspective.
transcript.translation: 但是，正如罗斯林在其著作《事实》中指出的，正确看待所有坏消息是很重要的。

transcript.text: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle-class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line.
transcript.translation: 尽管近几十年来全球化确实对发达经济体的中产阶级工资产生了一些下行压力，但它也帮助了数亿人摆脱了全球贫困线。

transcript.text: If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
transcript.translation: 如果我们真正关心全球福祉，全球化是确保经济繁荣由所有国家共享，而不仅仅是少数发达经济体享有的唯一途径。

transcript.text: While some people glorify the past, one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently a significant part of the world's population lived in extreme poverty.
transcript.translation: 尽管有些人美化过去，但经济史的一个重大事实是，直到最近，世界人口的很大一部分仍生活在极端贫困中。

transcript.text: While there were many long-lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long-run growth rate is actually quite miraculous.
transcript.translation: 尽管有许多持久的起伏，比如大萧条或最近的大衰退，但长期增长率的持续性实际上相当神奇。

transcript.text: Low-income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades and are quickly catching up to the West.
transcript.translation: 包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家，近几十年来以显著更快的速度增长，并正在迅速赶上西方。

transcript.text: A 10% growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years.
transcript.translation: 长期保持10%的增长率意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。

transcript.text: It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
transcript.translation: 如果繁荣在全球范围内更广泛地分享，这显然是个好消息。

transcript.text: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades.
transcript.translation: 尽管由于全球化，国家内部的不平等有所上升，但全球不平等在过去几十年中一直呈稳步下降趋势。

transcript.text: This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people's living standards.
transcript.translation: 这主要是数亿人生活水平提高的结果。

transcript.text: In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
transcript.translation: 事实上，自工业革命以来，全球约一半的人口首次可以被视为中产阶级。

transcript.text: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful.
transcript.translation: 我们都知道嗅觉的力量很强大。

transcript.text: The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine.
transcript.translation: 例如，面包的香味可以像一台时光机。

transcript.text: One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago.
transcript.translation: 吸一口气，就能唤起多年前的记忆。

transcript.text: Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten.
transcript.translation: 确实，一般来说，气味分子能够复活那些早已被遗忘的记忆。

transcript.text: But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones?
transcript.translation: 但为什么气味有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感记忆？

transcript.text: The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories, and emotions are linked.
transcript.translation: 简而言之，是因为处理气味、记忆和情感的大脑区域是相互连接的。

transcript.text: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read.
transcript.translation: 气味是一种化学粒子，它漂浮进入鼻子，并到达负责嗅觉的大脑区域，在那里，感觉首先被处理成大脑可以识别的形式。

transcript.text: Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
transcript.translation: 然后，脑细胞将该信息传递到大脑中处理情感的区域，接着传递到相邻的进行学习和记忆形成的区域。

transcript.text: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain.
transcript.translation: 气味是唯一以如此直接的路径到达大脑情感和记忆中心的感觉。

transcript.text: That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories, and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
transcript.translation: 这导致了情感、记忆和气味之间的紧密联系，这就是为什么由气味触发的记忆比由视觉或声音触发的记忆更具情感色彩。

transcript.text: Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated.
transcript.translation: 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。

transcript.text: Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation, and then a memory might follow.
transcript.translation: 通常，当一个人闻到与其过去某个有意义事件相关的气味时，他们首先会对这种感觉产生情感反应，然后可能会想起相关的记忆。

transcript.text: But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface.
transcript.translation: 但有时，记忆并不会浮现出来。

transcript.text: The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past, but won't remember what they experienced.
transcript.translation: 这个人可能会感受到过去某件事的情感，但却想不起具体经历了什么。

transcript.text: What causes this baffling phenomenon?
transcript.translation: 是什么导致了这种令人困惑的现象？

transcript.text: The explanation is context.
transcript.translation: 解释是语境（或上下文）。

transcript.text: Imagine this scenario.
transcript.translation: 想象一下这个场景。

transcript.text: A person is walking down the street, smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response.
transcript.translation: 一个人走在街上，闻到一种几十年前第一次闻到的气味，这引发了一种情感反应。

transcript.text: If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
transcript.translation: 如果那个人最初是在一个非常不同的语境下遇到那种气味的，那么要找回相关的记忆就会困难得多，因为大脑使用语境来赋予信息意义并找到那个记忆。

transcript.text: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories.
transcript.translation: 尽管由气味唤起的记忆具有特殊性，但它们与其他记忆有着相同的缺点。

transcript.text: They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time.
transcript.translation: 它们并不总是准确的，并且会随着时间而改变。

transcript.text: In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted.
transcript.translation: 事实上，每次我们回忆某件事，那个记忆都可能变得扭曲。

transcript.text: But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
transcript.translation: 但是，由于这些记忆唤起了强烈的情感关联，那些因气味而想起某事的人常常坚信记忆是准确的，即使事实并非如此。

paragraphs.text: Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? Negative energy can then cast a __26__ over your efforts to build a shared understanding.

paragraphs.text: In fact, collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. Strong listening skills are essential. Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, __27__ smiles, and warm comments helps. So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue __28__ from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate __29__.
paragraphs.translation: 事实上，协作解决问题的对话需要技巧。强大的倾听技巧至关重要。通过欣赏、亲切的微笑和温暖的评论注入积极因素有所帮助。保持情绪基调处于冷静区域的基本能力也同样重要。如果对话的基调升温并爆发愤怒，对话就会从协作转向对抗，进展可能立即停止。

paragraphs.text: In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry.
paragraphs.translation: 此外，有效的对话通常还有一个重要特征：对称性。

paragraphs.text: Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. Are you each getting equal airtime? When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to become annoying to one or both of you. The silent partner __30__ tires of only listening, while the talker can feel __31__. Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.
paragraphs.translation: 对话中的对称性指的是每个参与者说话量的平衡。你们是否获得了平等的发言时间？当一个参与者主导大部分谈话时，这种不对称或缺乏平衡往往会让一方或双方感到烦恼。沉默的一方通常会厌倦只倾听，而说话者可能会感到负担过重。通常，双方都更倾向于更平等的交流。

paragraphs.text: Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can __32__ symmetry as well. The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor.
paragraphs.translation: 不同的语速和音量水平也会破坏对称性。语速更快或声音更大的一方很容易占据更多发言时间。语速较慢或声音较轻的一方可能难以获得发言机会。

paragraphs.text: Conversations also lose balance when one partner's opinions count more than the other's. One person's input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more __33__. One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more __34__.
paragraphs.translation: 当一方的意见比另一方更重要时，对话也会失去平衡。一个人的输入可能更具影响力，因为其表达方式更有力。一个观点可能容易被忽略，因为它的表达更试探性。

paragraphs.text: If either partner fairly consistently __35__ or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive.
paragraphs.translation: 如果任何一方相当持续地主导或消失，调整这种模式将是有帮助的。对话会感觉更有成效，同时整体关系也可能感觉更积极。

material.title: What is a super blood wolf moon?

paragraphs.text: Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.
paragraphs.translation: 蓝月、玫瑰月、超级月亮。不知何故，所有网站似乎都认为你真的想了解这些月亮。一个标题会宣称：“赶上本周末的惊艳超级月亮。”另一个则会抱怨：“超级月亮其实没什么大不了的，你们都在破坏天文学。”

paragraphs.text: The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
paragraphs.translation: 最新的例子是超级血狼月食，这听起来像我在九年级时会为一首情感歌曲表演现代舞的名字，但实际上，这是一个定于1月20日发生的天文事件。正如我们下面将解释的，这个月亮并没有真正神秘或特别之处，它不会看起来像天空中血腥的狼头或任何狂野的东西。我们通过将历史上用来追踪全年满月的所有修饰词拼凑在一起，得到了这些超级月球事件，在互联网时代，我们可能会有点过于热情。

paragraphs.text: Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
paragraphs.translation: 请将此视为所有观月新闻的首选资源。以下是关于最新月球事件你需要知道的信息。

paragraphs.text: Look, it's okay if you don't know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.
paragraphs.translation: 听着，如果你不知道也没关系。可能有很多人四处走动，假装他们完全知道为什么天空中的那个东西似乎会定期变大和变小，但他们其实完全不知道。

paragraphs.text: The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
paragraphs.translation: 月球绕地球运行，并且是潮汐锁定的——这意味着它总是向我们展示同一面，而不是像我们的行星那样旋转。这就是为什么即使月球在我们周围旋转，你总能看到月球上的人（或月兔，取决于你的文化偏好）。但是，虽然满月时月亮在天空中又大又亮，但这只是因为它反射了太阳的光。但月球总是在移动，所以它从不同角度受到阳光照射。在新月时，它对我们是看不见的，因为我们的卫星正好位于我们和太阳之间；所谓的月球暗面像拉斯维加斯一样明亮，但我们能看到的一面处于阴影中。当地球正好位于太阳和月球之间时，发生满月，所以阳光照射到我们能看到的部分。而所有其他月相只是从一个极端过渡到另一个极端。

paragraphs.text: The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee (近地点), and the most distant point is apogee (远地点). 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
paragraphs.translation: 月球并不总是与地球保持完全相同的距离，因为它的轨道不是完美的圆形。我们称最近点为近地点，最远点为远地点。2018年，最近的近地点和最远的远地点都发生在1月，差异大约为30,000英里。

paragraphs.text: The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
paragraphs.translation: 你关心这个普通距离变化的原因是它使月亮变得超级。当满月发生在靠近近地点时，它看起来会大一点。老实说，差异并不那么显著，但如果你能在拍摄超级月亮时旁边放一个物体来显示规模的轻微增加，它可能看起来很酷。1月的超级血狼月食之所以超级，是因为日期与月球在1月最接近我们的时间一致，但月球实际上要到2月的超级月亮才会达到今年的最近点，你可以预期会有大量不必要的兴奋。

paragraphs.text: Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
paragraphs.translation: 血月只发生在月全食期间（在任何给定地点，每年可能发生几次）。当月球滑入我们的阴影时，我们给它一个红色的色调。月球在升起或落下时，或者如果整晚都低垂在地平线上，也可能看起来是橙色的——从它反射的光必须穿过那里更厚的大气层，这会散射更多的蓝光。但你可能只会在月食期间看到那种深邃、阴森的红色。

paragraphs.text: A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
paragraphs.translation: 很多关于月亮的标题都很荒谬（你不需要对蓝月特别兴奋，它看起来就像普通的满月），但如果血月在你的地区可见，你绝对应该起床去看看，尽管它们只是月食，而不是天神之间血腥战斗的证据。

paragraphs.text: In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
paragraphs.translation: 2018年3月，我们有了当年的第二个“蓝月”，广受好评。虽然这不一定是以一种“天哪，快出去看看”的方式特别，但它确实是特别的：蓝月是当两个满月出现在同一个日历月时的昵称，自1999年以来，我们之前没有在一年中有两个蓝月。要到2037年才会再次发生。天文学家大卫·查普曼解释说，这只是我们日历的一个特性；一旦我们停止基于月亮做事，开始尝试遵循太阳和季节，我们就不再每月有一个可靠的满月。月球周期平均为29.53天，所以在大多数月份，我们仍然只有一个新月和一个满月。但偶尔，一个月会从另一个月偷走一个满月。在2018年（以及1999年，再到2037年），1月和3月都在月首和月末堆叠了满月，让2月处于黑暗中。

paragraphs.text: Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue." Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
paragraphs.translation: 一年有两个蓝月是罕见的，但我们每隔几年就有单个蓝月。另外，有趣的事实：实际上不是蓝色的。月亮确实可以呈现出忧郁的蓝色，但这只有在大小正好的颗粒分散在天空中时才会发生——这与月亮作为“蓝月”的状态无关。火山爆发或火灾产生的大团灰烬可以做到这一点，但这并不经常发生，而且要让两个如此罕见的情况同时发生，无疑需要星星对齐。

paragraphs.text: You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
paragraphs.translation: 你可能听说2018年超级特别的第二个蓝月也是逾越节月亮。这是真的！这意味着它是春天的第一个满月，通常用于确定复活节星期日的日期。所有这些只是日历上的胡闹，我们拒绝进一步探讨。

paragraphs.text: Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the U.S. alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.
paragraphs.translation: 有时你会看到一个标题，承诺一个带有如此多修饰词的月亮，让你头晕目眩。也许是超级蓝血虫月？或者是超级血狼月？很多网站会告诉你，“狼月”是“美洲原住民”文化中一年第一个满月的传统名称，鉴于今天仅在美国就有573个注册的部落国家，更不用说历史上，这是一种奇怪的说法。认为饥饿的嚎叫的狼在1月是如此普遍，以至于所有具有不同文化、地理和语言的北美地区都自发地想出相同的昵称，这是不合逻辑的。

paragraphs.text: Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.
paragraphs.translation: 许多文化对给定月份或季节的满月有传统名称，所以如果你试图真正充实一个关于比平均稍大月亮观景的故事，有一个相当长的列表可供选择。但这些都是基于人类日历、活动和民间传说；你不会在4月外出看到粉红月亮，尽管我希望如此。

paragraphs.text: With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.
paragraphs.translation: 随着人口增长和全球城市化不断加速，人们关注城市的可持续性，却很少关注乡村。

paragraphs.text: Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
paragraphs.translation: 乡村生活与紧密联系的社区、归属感和简单宁静的生活相关。然而，尽管乡村中存在这些元素的部分或全部，但也存在保守主义和就业机会的缺乏。正是由于后者，乡村社区正在遭受困境。受城市地区经济改善的吸引，世界各地的乡村居民正在迁出，导致人口密集城市的过度拥挤，并使乡村陷入荒凉。

paragraphs.text: So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes, or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，乡村如何能在这些变化中确保其生存，或者它应该生存吗？由于住宅和设施之间的距离以及公共交通的频繁中断，乡村居民更依赖汽车。乡村居民还需要更多能源来维护他们大多独立的建筑。在城市里，我们可能像盒子一样堆叠，但这带来了乡村无法匹配的能源效率。乡村的能源需求导致人均碳排放高于城市，因此支持这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。

paragraphs.text: Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
paragraphs.translation: 保护乡村是一个热门话题。那些在城市中发财的人经常在乡村购买第二套住房，间歇性地访问以体验所谓的简单生活。这样做的副作用是，由于需求增加，房价被推高，使得当地人难以负担。这一挑战的解决方案尚未找到，因为市场力量进一步迫使居民离开乡村。对于那些相信乡村保护的人来说，这是令人遗憾的。

paragraphs.text: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a 'global village'. Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管对乡村的理想化观点很常见，但现实是乡村生活一直在不断演变。工业化带来了劳动分工的增加，改变了乡村居民之间的社会联系。互联网将曾经陌生的文化引入了乡村。改善的旅行连接和可负担性使世界更加易于接触，创造了一个“地球村”。考虑到这些变化，一个不断演变的乡村无疑是不可避免的。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
paragraphs.translation: 也许乡村也应该为未来大规模人口增长做好准备。随着世界各地城市的快速发展，当前的城市一代将如何应对大规模城市化不可避免的社会变化？对简单生活的渴望会变得更强烈，从而推动乡村复兴吗？

paragraphs.text: As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.
paragraphs.translation: 随着世界继续城市化，呼吁保护乡村的声音可能会越来越大。但变化是不可避免的。我们知道世界将看到新城市从尘埃中崛起，现有城市成长为特大城市，但乡村的未来则不那么清晰。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder (观看者)," are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
paragraphs.translation: 陈述，如“美在观看者眼中”，很少受到质疑。它们已深深嵌入我们的意识中，以至于人们认为否则的想法是荒谬的。然而，至少反驳这一假设可能是有用的，因为人们会从审美角度评估环境、情境和人物。我们可能发现我们仍然相信它是正确的，但也可能发现情况比你想象的要复杂得多。

paragraphs.text: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
paragraphs.translation: 最近一项探索审美品味的研究发表在《Cognition》杂志上。该研究结果表明，人们对自然物体的审美评价非常一致，但对人工制品或人造物体的分歧更大。

paragraphs.text: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
paragraphs.translation: 研究发现，共享品味在面部和自然景观中最为常见，但在建筑和艺术作品中最不常见。假说是常见的愉悦特征，如比例或对称性，在起作用。

paragraphs.text: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
paragraphs.translation: 对自然场景的偏好可能通过生活经验习得。随着人们成长，可能更倾向于宜居性、安全性和开放性等因素。景观的细节会变化，但基础更常见，例如水、开放空间和关怀的迹象。

paragraphs.text: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
paragraphs.translation: 艺术和建筑，不同于自然空间，没有相同的接触程度。因此，人们没有相同水平的共享品味。

paragraphs.text: It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than 'behavioral consequences.'
paragraphs.translation: 人工制品共享品味中较低的共识程度可能更多地与风格元素有关，而不是“行为后果”。

paragraphs.text: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
paragraphs.translation: 所有后果似乎都合理（或至少可能），但我认为可能有一个有趣的哲学结论他们没有得出。似乎我们的审美偏好或评价存在客观基础。我并不是说这意味着美是完全客观的，只是可能存在一般客观原则在起作用，即美不仅仅在观看者眼中。

paragraphs.text: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
paragraphs.translation: 自然以一种常见的方式在世界各地展现出一些普遍的审美特征，如光辉。它并非完全相同，但很常见。例如，不同地方的日落足够相似，几乎具有普遍吸引力。

paragraphs.text: Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
paragraphs.translation: 可能的美之普遍原则——如比例、适宜性、光辉等——是宽泛的类别，允许各种体现方式。当人们参与建筑或艺术中的人工制品制作时，他们以独特的方式应用这些非常普遍的概念。但他们应用原则的方式可能不具有普遍吸引力。

paragraphs.text: This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.
paragraphs.translation: 这就是为什么体验不同文化及其人工制品很重要，因为它使我们能够接触或构建美的不同方式。而且质疑我们的假设总是好的。

questionGroups.sourceText: 洋山港(Yangshan Port)是上海航运中心的重要组成部分，是中国第一个深水港，也是世界上规模最大的深水港之一。经过近20年的发展，洋山港已实现高度自动化。数字技术和人工智能的使用大大减少了用工成本和碳排放。自主研发的码头管理系统可以在百公里之外对大型设备进行远程操控。洋山港看上去一片繁忙，现场却见不到人工操作，而且能够24小时不间断运作。洋山港将不断发展，为把上海建成一个全球航运中心做出更大贡献。

answer.modelTranslation: Yangshan Port, an important component of the Shanghai shipping center, is China's first deep-water port and one of the largest deep-water ports in the world. After nearly two decades of development, Yangshan Port has achieved a high degree of automation. The use of digital technology and artificial intelligence has greatly reduced labor costs and carbon emissions. Its independently developed terminal management system can remotely control large equipment from hundreds of kilometers away. Although Yangshan Port looks extremely busy, no manual operation can be seen on site, and it is able to run around the clock without interruption. Yangshan Port will keep developing and make greater contributions to building Shanghai into a global shipping center.
